children: investigation of transactions involving Fortis, IHH Healthcare and RHT Health Trust Indu Bhan New Delhi: Fortis Healthcare Ltd (FHL) on Wednesday moved the Supreme Court against the Delhi High Court's order directing a forensic audit of transactions between the hospital chain, a business trust floated by its former promoters Malvinder Singh and Shivinder Singh, and Malaysia's IHH Healthcare Berhad.

The high court, in its August 31 ruling related to Japanese drugmaker Daiichi Sankyo's petition seeking execution of a 3,500 crore Singapore arbitration award it won against the Singh brothers, directed that every person and transaction linked to Fortis' deal with IHH Healthcare be covered in the audit.

Terming the HC's findings while ordering the audit as "highly prejudicial" against it, FHL told the SC that it was "a complete stranger to the (arbitration) award, not a party to the arbitration and admittedly not a judgment debtor or garnishee, and cannot be made one through the execution proceedings" filed by Daiichi Sankyo.

Only the Singh brothers and their respective families and family-owned and controlled companies were parties to the arbitration, FHL stated in the appeal filed through counsel Sanya Sud. FHL, IHH that now hold a controlling stake in the hospital chain and its about 250,000 public shareholders were not directly, indirectly or even remotely involved in or parties to the arbitration/recovery proceedings, it argued.

The HC directions constitute an open-ended, roving and fishing inquiry, and violate well-established principles of company law that no attribution (i.e., holding a company responsible for the acts of its directors) can apply to a public listed company, it said. The order "has a devastating effect on corporate and arbitration law in India" and the petitioner, the company said.

The company is virtually found liable for acts and wrongdoings of its erstwhile rogue shareholder-promoters undertaken in their personal capacity, it said. The IHH investment came nine months after the complete exit of the erstwhile "rogue shareholders" and their proxy companies, the petition stated. FHL told the SC that there was no purchase of its shares by IHH from the Singh brothers, their family members or companies.

IHH acquired a 31% stake in FHL in July 2018 for 4,000 crore through the bidding route for fresh shares. Its open offer for another 26% did not happen after the Supreme Court put on hold the sale of FHL to IHH following Daiichi's contempt plea against the Singhs. FHL itself is a victim of the Singh brothers' "fraud and embezzlement", Sud said.

The HC directions were passed on pleas filed by Daiichi while pursuing enforcement of the arbitration award it won against the Singhs, whom it accused of concealing information when they sold Ranbaxy Laboratories to the Japanese company for $4.6 billion in 2008. Daiichi challenged the Fortis deal with IHH, arguing that it caused dissipation of the Singh brothers' assets which should have been used to pay the arbitral award. The audit would also cover the sale of pledged FHL shares by 17 lenders in the open market in 2018, around the time IHH was bidding for the company stake. Yes Bank this week filed an appeal in the top court against the high court order.

title: Fortis Moves SC Over HC's Forensic Audit Order
